diagnostic_evidence.quote: In each substep, we employ the second-order IMEX scheme discussed above.

issues.failure_explanation: The Strang substeps 1, 2, 4, 5 each evolve over a half step (e.g. the first K/S-substeps cover [t^n, t^{n+1/2}]). The stated second-order IMEX pattern (eq:stage_coupled--eq:step_coupled) anchors its implicit trapezoidal rule at the endpoints of its own step, which for these half-substeps would be E^n and E^{n+1/2}. Instead, all four half-step corrector equations pair the trapezoid with the full-step fields L_h^n and L_h^{n+1}, one of which lies outside each half-substep's interval (E^{n+1} for the first K/S-substeps, E^n for the second K/S-substeps); moreover the implicit-Euler predictors use E^{n+1/2} at a node t^n + dt/4 where no field is computed. So the displayed half-step equations are not the second-order IMEX scheme applied on their own intervals, and the advertised second-order (and stiff-accuracy) guarantee of Algorithm alg:second_order is not supported by the construction as written. (The central L-step, spanning the full step, is consistent.)
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Re-derive the half-step sub-equations with fields anchored at each half-substep's own endpoints: either predict/compute the additional field values needed at the half-substep nodes (extra density predictions plus Poisson solves, reusing the existing machinery), or explicitly restate the scheme as a field-frozen variant and weaken the second-order claim accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised second-order temporal accuracy of the second-order low-rank scheme (and the AP behavior reported for it) is unsupported: the half-step sub-equations as written carry an O(Delta t) temporal misalignment of the implicit field nodes, so the second-order designation of alg:second_order is unproven.
issues.title: Second-order scheme's half-step sub-equations use implicit field nodes outside their substep intervals
issues.why_classification: The repair is contained (re-specifying the four half-step field nodes with existing machinery, or restating the scheme as a field-frozen variant with a correspondingly limited order claim); the method, architecture, and a recognizably comparable second-order construction survive, so this is more than minor but not a major loss.

issues.failure_explanation: With the paper's discrete norms, the constant velocity function bar(u) has norm ||bar u * 1||_v^h = sqrt(L_v)|bar u|, not |bar u|. From the displayed Cauchy-Schwarz estimate |bar u| <= sqrt(L_v M_max)||u - bar u||_v^h one obtains ||u||_v^h <= (1 + L_v sqrt(M_max))||u - bar u||_v^h, which is weaker than the displayed final inequality with constant (1 + sqrt(L_v M_max))^2 (the factor sqrt(L_v) is silently dropped). Hence the displayed chain does not establish the coercivity constant gamma_h as explicitly defined; the constant is only recoverable by sharpening the intermediate step to ||M||_v^{h,2} <= M_max (valid since <M,1>_v^h = 1).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Sharpen the displayed intermediate bound to ||M||_v^{h,2} <= M_max * <1,M>_v^h = M_max (justified by the assumed normalization <M,1>_v^h = 1); the triangle step then yields exactly the displayed constant (1 + sqrt(L_v M_max))^2 and the proposition holds verbatim.
issues.overall_effect: The explicitly stated coercivity constant gamma_h of Proposition prop:coercivity is not established by the proof as written; the downstream Assumption asm:small_fluct and Theorem thm:main_AP, which are stated in terms of 'the coercivity constant from Proposition prop:coercivity', remain valid once the (true, sharp) constant is supplied, so no formal result is lost.
issues.title: Coercivity constant's norm-comparison step is invalid: a sqrt(L_v) factor is silently dropped
issues.why_classification: A one-line standard sharpening of the Cauchy-Schwarz step (using the normalization already assumed) completes the proof; every stated constant, the assumption regime, and the main theorem survive unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof claims L_h factors as beta (x) T^(alpha) plus beta^{-1} (x) T^(1/alpha) with T^(alpha)w = (alpha_{q+1/2}(w_{q+1}-w_q) - alpha_{q-1/2}(w_q-w_{q-1}))/Delta v^2 and an analogous T^(1/alpha) (written with u in place of w). The actual stencil eq:fp_discrete_separable splits into two-point factors (alpha_{q+1/2} w_{q+1} - alpha_{q-1/2} w_q)/Delta v^2 and (alpha_{q-1/2}^{-1} w_{q-1} - alpha_{q+1/2}^{-1} w_q)/Delta v^2; expanding the displayed three-point operators with the beta/beta^{-1} weights produces extra cross terms (e.g. -alpha_{q+1/2} beta_p w_q + alpha_{q-1/2} beta_p w_{q-1} in the first factor) that are not in L_h. Moreover the claimed induced norms ||T^(alpha)|| <= 2 alpha_max/Delta v^2 are false for the displayed three-point operators (for constant alpha their l^2-induced norms reach ~4 alpha_max/Delta v^2). The proof's decomposition and norm estimates therefore fail as written; the proposition's stated bound remains true for the genuine two-point stencil factors, which satisfy exactly the displayed norm bounds.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Redefine the velocity factors as the stencil's actual two-point operators T^(alpha): (alpha_{q+1/2} w_{q+1} - alpha_{q-1/2} w_q)/Delta v^2 and T^(1/alpha): (alpha_{q-1/2}^{-1} w_{q-1} - alpha_{q+1/2}^{-1} w_q)/Delta v^2 (fixing the u/w typo); the triangle-inequality row estimates then give precisely the claimed norms 2 alpha_max/Delta v^2 and 2/(alpha_min Delta v^2) and the constant kappa_h stands.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of Proposition prop:fluctuation_bound is invalid as written (its operator decomposition and induced-norm estimates are false for the operators it displays); the statement itself, the constant kappa_h in eq:kappa_h_def, and Theorem thm:main_AP's use of it remain valid once the two-point stencil factors are used.
issues.title: Fluctuation-bound proof decomposes the stencil into velocity operators that do not match the stencil and whose claimed norms are false
issues.why_classification: A local, routine repair (define the difference operators as the stencil's actual two-point factors) restores the proof verbatim with the same constant kappa_h; no claim, rate, or guarantee of the paper changes.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose asserts a kinetic left part and a fluid right part. Evaluating the prescribed function: at x = -1, tanh(5+10x) = tanh(-5) ~ -1, so epsilon(-1) = eps_0 + 1/2(tanh 15 + tanh(-5)) is approximately 1.0e-3, i.e. of order eps_0, not order one; eps(x) is O(1) only on a middle-left band (roughly x >= -0.5 up to the cutoff 0.3), and at x = 0.3 the left piece still gives eps ~ 0.98 before the definition jumps to eps_0 for x > 0.3. The prescribed profile therefore has a small-eps region at BOTH ends and an O(1) band in the middle-left, contradicting the claimed kinetic-left/fluid-right layout.

failure_location.quote: so that the left part of the domain has $\varepsilon(x)$ of order one, while the right part has a smaller, nearly constant value $\varepsilon(x)\approx \varepsilon_0$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the description of the profile (kinetic only for x roughly in [-0.5, 0.3], small eps near both domain ends, with a jump at x = 0.3), or replace the prescribed eps(x) by a profile that actually realizes the stated left-kinetic/right-fluid layout.
issues.overall_effect: The description of the mixed-regime test's kinetic/fluid layout is materially misleading; readers are told the left part of the domain is kinetic when the prescribed profile is small near x = -1 and O(1) only in a middle band with a jump at x = 0.3, affecting the interpretation of the reported density/field/error profiles.
issues.title: Mixed-regime prose mischaracterizes the prescribed epsilon(x) profile
issues.why_classification: The prescribed formula itself is used as given in the experiments; only the accompanying characterization is false, so a local prose correction preserves every setup, computation, and reported result.
